journey: Arabic text in a native (non-Flatpak) Chromium/Electron app (VS Code 1.145.2) on Oracle with an English or other non-Arabic UI locale.
owner_observation: Owner asked to fix Meyar on Oracle; the live VS Code chat painted Arabic in a non-Meyar face (local private capture, not committed).
live_renderer_before: Owner's VS Code renderer processes mapped /usr/share/fonts/paktype-naqsh/PakTypeNaqsh.ttf (no Meyar Arabic).
mechanism: Blink/Chromium per-character fallback on Linux queries a pattern with only FC_LANG (UI locale). 00-moos-meyar-defaults.conf aliases only the generic sans-serif, which 49-sansserif appends after those aliases ran; 61-moos-brand's sans-serif alias is weak, so FC_LANG ranks first: fonts declaring both en and ar (PakType Naqsh) win for an English UI.
change: A pattern rule at the top of 00-moos-meyar-defaults.conf assigns strong sans-serif only when the pattern has no family value (qual=all against a sentinel string), before the existing generic aliases.

fontconfig_controls.fixture: tests/native_meyar_fontconfig.py (native fonts.conf normalization, source fonts/policy, private cache)

native_electron_control.result: old maps PakType Naqsh and no Meyar Arabic; fixed maps Meyar Arabic and no PakType Naqsh. Mapped files are not pixel acceptance.
native_electron_control.cleanup: all private instance processes verified gone; one empty /tmp profile directory left for reboot cleanup (rm was refused)

live_copy.readback: system fc-match :lang=en/en-us/de/fr/ar first Arabic = Meyar Arabic; sans-serif:lang=ar Meyar Sans, monospace Meyar Mono, serif:lang=ar Noto Naskh Arabic, Noto Sans:lang=en Noto Sans unchanged
live_copy.retirement: becomes unmodified once a booted signed image ships identical bytes; otherwise restore /usr/etc copy

not_qualified: Which face paints owner VS Code chat Arabic after reboot (maps Noto Sans Arabic; Meyar Arabic is a Noto Sans Arabic derivative, so pixels differ mainly in dots)
Owner VS Code painted pixels after restart/reboot
Flatpak Chrome/Chromium: runtime fontconfig and the MoOS per-app policy intentionally carry no generic defaults (earlier refusal retained)
named-family+lang=en fontconfig queries (Skia matchFamilyStyleCharacter path) still rank PakType first; Blink on Linux does not use it for per-character fallback

post_reboot_readback.etc_copy: /etc keeps 650e418c over pristine /usr/etc bfa123db after the staged-deployment /etc merge
post_reboot_readback.fontconfig: fc-match -s :lang=en first Arabic-covering face = Meyar Arabic
post_reboot_readback.owner_vscode: Owner VS Code (started after reboot) maps NotoSansArabic Regular/SemiBold/Bold and no PakType Naqsh; the chat Arabic now paints a regular naskh-sans face instead of the Urdu face (local private capture).
post_reboot_readback.system_ui_finding: VS Code's Linux workbench stack is system-ui, Ubuntu, Droid Sans, sans-serif. fc-match must escape it (system\-ui; an unescaped '-' parses as size and asked for family 'system'). Live system\-ui resolves to Cantarell. A strong system-ui alias to Meyar passed fixture controls, but isolated VS Code trees under current and system-ui policies mapped identical faces (Meyar Arabic and Noto Sans Arabic both), so the painted family was not established. It was withdrawn from this change; it needs glyph-family readback (e.g. CDP CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode or private-KWin pixels) before shipping.
